Subject: ACME POC: evaluation methodology & success criteria

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and a proposed POC plan so we can align on success criteria and ownership: 

High-level ask from ACME: evaluate Redwood for customer support automation (intent classification + response generation) across your staging traffic. 

Proposed POC structure (suggested):
- Offline evaluation (2 weeks): run historical ticket set through Redwood models, measure accuracy/fidelity against labeled responses.
- Online shadow (1 week): mirror a subset of live staging traffic to Redwood; no customer-facing responses. Monitor end-to-end latency, safety flags, and model quality.
- Optional short production pilot after success criteria met.

Suggested success criteria (first pass):
- Macro accuracy / rubric score >= 0.92 on offline eval (see attached rubric)
- End-to-end median latency < 350ms for shadowed requests
- Safety flag rate <= threshold (TBD together)
- Cost target: competitive unit cost (we'll provide an estimate)

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood: Marissa (PM, commercial), Dylan (technical lead / infra ops)
- ACME: Priya (product lead), Alex (engineering lead)

Timing: target start the week of Dec 7, 2026. Total duration: ~3 weeks (2w offline, 1w shadow).

Next steps:
1) Confirm owners and timeline
2) Agree on offline eval data set and rubric (I attached a draft rubric + success criteria spreadsheet)
3) Procurement contact for SOW / SOC/MSA details

Attachments: acme-poc-success-criteria.xlsx, redwood-eval-rubric.pdf

If that matches your expectations, I can send a short SOW and a calendar invite to kick off alignment next week.

Best,
Marissa

Great notes — happy to adjust. Attached a Google Doc link in the drive and the rubric PDF; also attached the success criteria spreadsheet with thresholds filled in for initial discussion. Quick clarifications: 

Offline eval metrics (examples in rubric):
- Rubric score (weighted): intent detection 40%, response relevance 40%, style/brand match 20%
- Target rubric score >= 0.92 (we can iterate)
- Precision/recall for high-priority intents >= 0.9

Online / shadow metrics:
- End-to-end median latency < 350ms (99th percentile target < 700ms)
- Rate of safety flags / escalation to human < 1%
- Real-time quality checks: random sample of 100 requests/day for human review during shadow

Ownership and ops: 
- Redwood provides a temporary staging endpoint, KV caching configs, and a dashboard (we'll share access)
- Dylan to coordinate the traffic mirroring and logging format

Proposed updated timeline: 
- Week of Dec 7: kickoff + dataset handoff
- Weeks of Dec 14-27: offline evaluation + weekly checkpoints
- Weeks of Jan 4-17: online shadow (2 weeks) — per Alex's ask

Can ACME confirm: 
- Which historical dataset subset we should use for offline (date ranges / ticket volume)?
- Any PII redaction needs or masking rules?

I'll draft the SOW and send for signatures once procurement confirms billing terms.

Thanks — attaching: redwood-eval-rubric.pdf, acme-poc-success-criteria.xlsx

Cheers,
Marissa
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME POC: evaluation methodology & success criteria

Quick technical follow-up from our side: 

For the online shadow we will need the staging mirror to include a header that preserves request IDs and anonymized user IDs so we can trace requests end-to-end. We'll also expect JSON payload with the following fields: request_id, text, metadata (timestamp, channel). I can share a small schema.

Traffic/sample size: to get stable signals we recommend ~5k shadowed requests/day for two weeks (so ~70k total); if ACME wants a lighter sample we can scope down.

Data handling: Redwood will not persist raw PII beyond short-term logs used for debugging. We'll support customer-managed keys (KMS) if required and can redact fields at the mirror level if ACME prefers. Please confirm any compliance constraints (e.g., no PII in mirrored payloads).

Monitoring: we'll send a dashboard invite (Grafana + per-route metrics) and nightly aggregate reports. Dylan will own the infra runbook during the POC.

Action items for ACME:
- Confirm sample traffic rate (5k/day vs. lower)
- Confirm whether mirrored payloads will be pre-redacted
- Provide procurement contact for SOW/terms if different from procurement@acme.com

Thanks — happy to sync on a short call next week to walk through schema.

— Dylan
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
